correctness.rationale: A convex spiral center cannot lie on or outside the unit disk because the support directions then leave a zero-mass angular gap of length at least pi; positive mass of every basic sector forces that gap into at most two adjacent sectors, whose combined angle is then greater than pi, contradicting wedge convexity. For an interior center, radial projection preserves cyclic order, so equal arclength masses force regular 3k-gon intersection points. For each (k+1)-wedge the determinant of its endpoint rays is exactly 2 sin(Delta/2) times the signed distance to one chord-midpoint support line. Thus all convexity constraints are precisely the half-planes of a regular 3k-gon. The radius, area, union-over-rotations, intersection-over-rotations, and limits then follow by elementary regular-polygon geometry.

value.rationale: The recent theorem is existential for every mass, so a canonical exactly solvable mass is a natural benchmark for understanding the geometry hidden by the topological proof. The uniform circle mass yields a complete, all-k moduli space rather than one example: all centers and phases are classified, the rigid k=2 case is recovered, and the feasible-center sets have explicit radii, area, and a nontrivial limiting disk. This provides a concrete structural model for the newly closed parameter family.
